LEG 1, metric label: reverting the Stripe call site to created ? ok : duplicate reddens exactly StripeWebhook_WhenInvoiceNumberRetriesExhaust_RecordsFailedNotDuplicateAndLeavesOrderUnpaid, 23 green, clean attribution and no collateral - held. But reverting the identical EuPlatesc call site ALONE leaves all 24 green, so only one of the two sites carries a test; the source is correct at both, this is a coverage gap not a live defect, and nothing else in the suite covers it because the exhausted path needs a real unique-constraint violation that EF InMemory cannot raise. A finer revert the fix round did not run, unwinding Status and PaidAt but leaving UpdatedAt, reddens it on UpdatedAt, so the pin the round-2 micro-review added is genuinely live now and not vacuous as it was at 08e7746. LEG 3, cancellation, is where this reopens. The catch widening is production code shipped with no test, and the resolution justifies that by saying forcing ReloadAsync to throw a cancellation needs a fake provider. That is false and was measured false: the Sentry.IHub mock this test file already builds fires CaptureEvent immediately before the reload, so a Callback that cancels a CancellationTokenSource passed as the request token makes ReloadAsync throw. A 45-line probe using only existing helpers passes with the fix and fails without it, OperationCanceledException escaping ReloadAsync through SqliteCommand.ExecuteReaderAsync and skipping RecordPaymentWebhook - exactly the defect the leg claims to close. The probe was removed and the tree restored before hand-back. Note that making the reload fail by any NON-cancellation means would not prove this leg, since such a test passes on both sides of the change. THREE QUESTIONS. Class: no-oping RecordPaymentWebhook reddens 14 of 24 tests in this area, and the sole metric-asserting survivor is Stripe_unhandled_event_type_records_nothing, which asserts absence by design - so no vacuous metric assertion survives here, unlike at 08e7746.
